segments: She pressed her forehead to the cold glass.
Outside, rain hammered on the window and the wind howled through the trees.
She thought of nothing at all.
He had said everything he came to say.
He stormed out, and the heavy oak door slammed shut behind him.
For a long moment nobody spoke.
The building was empty by then.
Her footsteps echoed down the long corridor.
She stopped at the last office and listened.
Somewhere, water was dripping into a sink.
They had waited ten years for this evening.
He raised his glass, and their glasses clinked across the table.
Nobody mentioned the letter.
She remembered the summer her father taught her to read.
He was patient in a way he never was again.
She kept the book for thirty years.
A gust of wind swept the empty street.
His footsteps were the only sound on the wet pavement.
Behind him a door slammed, and he did not turn around.
The rain began again.
